description: Society layer (devsim/population): the implicit population, ties, demography, opinions, institutions, economy and isolation feedback from 'MiroFish Society Layer: Corrected and Improved Design (v2)'. Tags: V = verified anchor (source named), D = design default, unverified, U = unverified figure from memory or the first report. Only V values may be cited as evidence; every other value is a tunable default. Each parameter carries its allowed range or choices.

grid.note: places form a grid x grid map of cells; population = grid^2 x cell_size

cell_size.note: people per cell (a neighborhood); candidate sets are this cell and its 8 neighbors

household_size.note: consecutive people in a cell form a household; housemates are kin and always tied

long_range_links.note: long-range candidate pairs per person and direction, from seeded permutations (weak far ties)

kappa.note: edge model scale: p_ij = min(1, kappa * theta_i * theta_j * exp(-|x_i - x_j| / h)); Karrer & Newman 2011 give the form (V), not the values

h.note: edge model length scale in latent units

theta_sigma.note: lognormal spread of the degree propensity theta (heavy-tailed degrees); Lindenfors et al. 2021 (V): no single network size, 95% intervals 2-336 and 4-520

theta_extraversion.note: theta multiplier exp(k * E z-score); the v1 source for Extraversion enlarging networks was off-topic

w_traits.note: latent weight of Big Five z-scores (homophily)

w_age.note: latent weight per year of age difference

w_dials.note: latent weight of the four dials

age_band_weights.note: share of people per 10-year age band 0-9 ... 80-89 at the start (a rough young pyramid, from memory)

tiers.note: Dunbar-style tiers by rank of tie strength (contact-frequency ranking, not a degree target; Lindenfors et al. 2021, V: 150 is unsupported as a constant)

strength_kin.note: starting strength of a kin (household) tie

strength_friend_mean.note: mean starting strength of a non-kin tie, raised for closer pairs in latent space

s_floor_kin.note: floor of a kin tie's decay (Roberts & Dunbar 2011, V: kin cost less to maintain; the value is not theirs)

s_floor_friend.note: floor of a friend tie's decay

stability_kin_days.note: S of a kin tie's shared memory; decay s(dt) = floor + (s_last - floor)(1 + dt/9S)^-1 reuses the memory forgetting curve

stability_friend_days.note: S of a friend tie's shared memory

contact_boost.note: a hostile contact lowers the tie's peak strength by this much (a friendly contact restores the tie to its peak; it never raises it)

contact_rehearsal_gain.note: S multiplied by 1 + gain per contact, like the memory rehearsal rule

contact_rate_max_per_year.note: recontact hazard of a pair at starting strength 1 (both directions together); rate = max * s0^exponent

contact_rate_exponent.note: how steeply contact frequency falls with weaker ties (s0 0.8 kin ~85/yr, 0.35 friend ~11/yr, 0.1 ~0.5/yr)

contact_extraversion.note: contact rate multiplier exp(k * E z-score)

contact_arousal_gain.note: contact rate multiplier 1 + k * arousal of the strongest shared memory

avoidance.note: contact rate multiplier exp(-k * threat_sensitivity * negativity of the shared memory)

hostile_rate_per_year.note: hostile contact hazard = rate * dysregulation * negativity of the shared memory

valence_friendly_gain.note: a friendly contact raises the shared memory's valence by this much

valence_hostile_drop.note: a hostile contact lowers the shared memory's valence by this much (and the tie by contact_boost)

rupture_per_hostile.note: chance a hostile contact ruptures the tie, growing with repeated hostility: 1 - exp(-k * hostile count)

reconcile_rate_per_year.note: reconciliation hazard after a rupture = rate * strength before the rupture

dial_mean.note: population means of the four dials

dial_sd.note: population spreads of the four dials

dial_neuroticism.note: shift per Neuroticism z-score (the sleep report: Neuroticism acts through the dials; no verified size)

infant_mortality_per_1000.note: NFHS-5 Maharashtra 2019-21 fact sheet: infant mortality per 1,000 live births (hazard for age 0-1)

under5_mortality_per_1000.note: NFHS-5 Maharashtra 2019-21: under-five mortality per 1,000 (with the infant figure, sets the age 1-5 hazard)

gompertz_makeham.note: adult death hazard per year from age 5: A + B exp(C age); not verified (the design found no India life table; check SRS life tables)

isolation_odds_ratio.note: Holt-Lunstad 2015: social isolation and mortality OR 1.29 (observational). Using it as a hazard multiplier is a design approximation

isolation_under65_factor.note: Holt-Lunstad 2015 (V): stronger effects in samples averaging under 65; the factor is a design default

integration_tier_weights.note: weight of a tie in the integration index by tier (1 = closest)

integration_reference.note: weighted tie sum that counts as fully integrated (index 1); isolation = 1 - index

median_age_first_marriage_women.note: NFHS-5 Maharashtra: median age at first marriage, women aged 20-49 (the only marriage input; the share married before 18 is a check)

marriage_ramp_women.note: shape of women's first-marriage hazard: zero before a, rising linearly to full at b, full until c, then falling exp(-(age-c)/d)

remarriage_factor.note: widowed women's marriage hazard relative to first marriage

spouse_age_gap.note: husband older by mean, sd, min, max years (from memory)

spouse_latent_scale.note: spouse choice weight exp(-latent distance / scale): compatibility by place, traits and dials

adolescent_fertility_per_1000.note: NFHS-5 Maharashtra: births per 1,000 women aged 15-19 (the only fertility input; total fertility 1.7 is a check)

fertility_shape.note: marital fertility: zero before a, flat to b, falling linearly to zero at c

parity_factors.note: birth hazard multiplier at parity 0, 1, 2, 3+ (stopping after two, e.g. sterilization; values not verified)

birth_interval_years.note: no further birth for this long after a birth

grief_mood_shift.note: mood-baseline shift from losing a tie of strength 1, buffered by the remaining closest ties (effect size not verified)

isolation_threat_per_year.note: threat sensitivity rise per year at full isolation (slow; effect size not verified)

opinion_epsilon.note: bounded-confidence threshold: two people move toward each other only if their opinions (on -1..1) differ by less than this; not verified, tune on your graph

opinion_mu.note: fraction of the gap each side moves (Deffuant); not verified

opinion_initial_sd.note: spread of starting opinions (normal, clipped to -1..1)

interaction_rate_per_year.note: opinion-relevant conversations per person per year, times exp(k * E)

interaction_extraversion.note: interaction rate multiplier exp(k * E z-score)

mean_field_bins.note: histogram bins for the opinion distribution of people not yet realized

mean_field_step_days.note: time step of the mean-field update (it stops early once the distribution settles)

credibility_gamma.note: acceptance weight = source credibility ^ (gamma * reality_testing): low reality testing accepts low-credibility sources

threat_rate_gain.note: threat-relevant items spread faster: rate x (1 + gain * threat_sensitivity)

contagion_window_days.note: exposures from distinct ties must fall within this window to count toward adoption

adoption_threshold_mean.note: mean distinct exposing ties needed to adopt a behavior (complex contagion, Centola & Macy, not opened); rumors use threshold 1

institution_types.note: lazy institutions: rules, a role-size distribution and a membership generator (no member list). Members are the region's eligible people whose hash picks this institution; roles go to the best fit (traits + seniority). All values are design defaults

norm_tightness_range.note: range a community's tightness is drawn from (Gelfand's tightness-looseness idea, not verified; no value for India or Pune is hardcoded)

norm_sd.note: spread of a community's accepted behavior around its norm

sanction_rate_per_year.note: sanction hazard (gossip, exclusion, tie rupture) = rate * tightness * visibility * distance from the norm in sds

sanction_sensitivity.note: one formula for everyone: sensitivity to sanction = logistic(bias + sum of weights x values); no archetype branch

collective_threshold.note: mean and sd of members' participation thresholds (Granovetter's threshold model, not opened)

collective_trigger_fraction.note: a collective event fires when the cascade reaches this share of members

job_initial_shares.note: unemployed, informal, formal shares at entry to working age (18)

job_rates_per_year.note: job-state Markov chain (PLFS transitions not verified)

job_trait_effects.note: Conscientiousness speeds moves out of unemployment and into formal work, exp(k C); Neuroticism speeds job loss, exp(k N)

income_median_monthly.note: median monthly income by state, rupees (from memory)

income_sigma.note: lognormal spread of income within a state

job_loss_shift.note: poverty-stress dial push on losing work (effect sizes not verified)

opportunity_rate_per_year.note: opportunities reaching a person per year, times 1 + k * institutions reachable through ties

opportunity_reach_gain.note: extra opportunity rate per distinct institution among a person's ties (knowing the right people)

opportunity_size_alpha.note: Pareto tail of opportunity sizes (heavy-tailed; Pluchino et al. 2018 use multiplicative events, V as a mechanism only)

opportunity_fit.note: chance to exploit = logistic(bias + O, C, E z-scores + log(1 + connections))

cooperation.note: chance allies cooperate = logistic(bias + k A): very low agreeableness costs allies

capital_gain.note: success multiplies capital by 1 + gain * size; set so a typical person roughly breaks even (median log-growth near 0), as in Pluchino et al.

capital_loss.note: failure multiplies capital by 1 - loss * min(1, size / 4)

bridge_top_ties.note: an engine character's closest ties that can reach them (contact news, context)

bridge_max_gap_days.note: longest wait between society checks for an engine character (deaths and fallings-out are noticed within this)

bridge_contact_news_max.note: at most this many 'got in touch' observations per check

topics.note: opinion topics the society layer tracks (names; each starts from the configured opinion spread)

bridge_contact_repeat_days.note: the same person getting in touch is news at most once in this many days (under the 30-day routine-reuse window, so repeats reuse their appraisal)
